```{r}
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(plotly))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(DT))

cars <- read_csv(
  "https://gist.githubusercontent.com/dvinubius/33486dad2dc86319f0a06ffdb1d4f34f/raw/",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  drop_na(
    Make, Model, Year, MSRP, `Engine HP`, `highway MPG`,
    `Vehicle Size`, `Vehicle Style`
  ) |>
  filter(MSRP > 0, `Engine HP` > 0, `highway MPG` > 0) |>
  mutate(
    highway_mpg = as.numeric(`highway MPG`),
    vehicle_size = `Vehicle Size`,
    vehicle_type = `Vehicle Style`,
    hover_label = paste0(
      "<b>", Make, " ", Model, " (", Year, ")</b>",
      "<br>Price: ", scales::dollar(MSRP, accuracy = 1),
      "<br>Horsepower: ", `Engine HP`, " hp",
      "<br>Highway fuel economy: ", highway_mpg, " MPG",
      "<br>Vehicle type: ", vehicle_type
    )
  )

price_power <- cars

price_power_correlation <- cor(price_power$MSRP, price_power$`Engine HP`)
power_fit <- lm(`Engine HP` ~ MSRP, data = price_power)
trend_line <- tibble(
  MSRP = seq(min(price_power$MSRP), max(price_power$MSRP), length.out = 100)
) |>
  mutate(predicted_hp = predict(power_fit, newdata = tibble(MSRP = MSRP)))

mpg_by_type <- cars |>
  group_by(vehicle_type) |>
  summarise(
    average_highway_mpg = mean(highway_mpg),
    vehicles = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(average_highway_mpg) |>
  mutate(
    vehicle_type = factor(vehicle_type, levels = vehicle_type),
    hover_label = paste0(
      "<b>", vehicle_type, "</b>",
      "<br>Average highway MPG: ", round(average_highway_mpg, 1),
      "<br>Vehicles: ", vehicles
    )
  )

best_mpg_type <- mpg_by_type |>
  slice_max(average_highway_mpg, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

balance_cars <- cars |>
  mutate(
    affordability_rank = 1 - percent_rank(MSRP),
    performance_rank = percent_rank(`Engine HP`),
    efficiency_rank = percent_rank(highway_mpg),
    balance_score = (
      affordability_rank + performance_rank + efficiency_rank
    ) / 3
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(balance_score), MSRP, desc(`Engine HP`), desc(highway_mpg))

top_balance <- balance_cars |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(
    hover_label = paste0(
      "<b>", Make, " ", Model, " (", Year, ")</b>",
      "<br>Price: ", scales::dollar(MSRP, accuracy = 1),
      "<br>Horsepower: ", `Engine HP`, " hp",
      "<br>Highway fuel economy: ", highway_mpg, " MPG",
      "<br>Balance score: ", round(balance_score, 3)
    )
  )

association_direction <- case_when(
  price_power_correlation > 0 ~ "positive",
  price_power_correlation < 0 ~ "negative",
  TRUE ~ "near zero"
)
```

## Are more expensive cars more powerful?

Across the `r format(nrow(price_power), big.mark = ",")` complete records, the
Pearson correlation between MSRP and horsepower is
**`r round(price_power_correlation, 2)`**. That is a
`r association_direction` association in this dataset, not a rule for every
vehicle and not evidence that price causes horsepower.

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = price_power,
  x = ~MSRP,
  y = ~`Engine HP`,
  color = ~vehicle_size,
  colors = c("#2A9D8F", "#E76F51", "#457B9D"),
  text = ~hover_label,
  hoverinfo = "text",
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(size = 7, opacity = 0.55)
) |>
  add_lines(
    data = trend_line,
    x = ~MSRP,
    y = ~predicted_hp,
    inherit = FALSE,
    name = "Linear trend",
    hoverinfo = "skip",
    line = list(color = "#263b77", width = 3)
  ) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Price (MSRP)", tickformat = "$,.0f"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Engine horsepower (hp)"),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Vehicle size")),
    hovermode = "closest"
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE)
```

## Which vehicle types get the best highway gas mileage?

Among the complete records, **`r as.character(best_mpg_type$vehicle_type[[1]])`**
has the highest average at **`r round(best_mpg_type$average_highway_mpg[[1]], 1)` MPG**
(`r format(best_mpg_type$vehicles[[1]], big.mark = ",")` records). These are
unadjusted averages, so vehicle age and other characteristics are not held
constant.

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = mpg_by_type,
  x = ~average_highway_mpg,
  y = ~vehicle_type,
  text = ~hover_label,
  hoverinfo = "text",
  type = "bar",
  orientation = "h",
  marker = list(color = "#2A9D8F")
) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Average highway fuel economy (MPG)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Vehicle type"),
    margin = list(l = 150)
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, displaylogo = FALSE)
```

## Which cars balance price, power, and fuel economy?

To make “balance” explicit, each complete record gets an equal-weight score:
the average of its percentile ranks for affordability (lower price ranks
higher), horsepower (higher ranks higher), and highway MPG (higher ranks
higher). These are the top-ranked records in this dataset by that definition,
not a universal best-car ranking.

```{r}
top_balance |>
  transmute(
    Year,
    Make,
    Model,
    MSRP,
    Horsepower = `Engine HP`,
    Highway_MPG = highway_mpg,
    Balance_score = balance_score
  ) |>
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = FALSE,
    colnames = c(
      "Year", "Manufacturer", "Model", "Price (MSRP)",
      "Horsepower (hp)", "Highway MPG", "Balance score"
    ),
    options = list(dom = "tip", pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
  ) |>
  DT::formatCurrency("MSRP", "$", digits = 0) |>
  DT::formatRound("Horsepower", 0) |>
  DT::formatRound("Highway_MPG", 0) |>
  DT::formatRound("Balance_score", 3)
```

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = top_balance,
  x = ~MSRP,
  y = ~highway_mpg,
  size = ~`Engine HP`,
  color = ~balance_score,
  colors = c("#E76F51", "#F4A261", "#2A9D8F"),
  text = ~hover_label,
  hoverinfo = "text",
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(opacity = 0.85)
) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Price (MSRP)", tickformat = "$,.0f"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Highway fuel economy (MPG)"),
    colorbar = list(title = "Balance score"),
    hovermode = "closest"
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE)
```
